operationalisation: The intervention works as a test of whether a duplicate display label corrupts an otherwise unchanged graph. At 16:00 on 18 September 2026, both targeted edges and the incidental Fiona Mora–Nina Beatrice Mercer control are supported in both files. Each edge retains exactly one materially distinct minimum proof route: a signed relationship confirmation joined to Desai’s exact-name reconciliation by the same intake reference. The intervention changes display-label uniqueness, not identity, kinship, or evidence eligibility. It does not by itself distinguish a correct reference join from a positional shortcut that happens to produce the same result.
source_diff: Only k9t2 changes: Q7-41 displays “Alexandra Rivera” in F0 and “Alex Rivera” in F1. M2-86 displays “Alex Rivera” and T9-53 displays “Nina Mercer” in both. Source IDs, titles, order, references, the column heading, and the 18 September 2026 14:40 BST export timestamp are unchanged. The forward audit accounts for every Source: r8h3 asserts parentage at Q7-41, j5x7 siblinghood at M2-86, and b2n6 parentage at T9-53; c7v4 resolves those three references and records the engagement and intake procedure; k9t2 adds administrative labels and a recorded staff role. In reverse, Alexandra Inez Rivera leads only through Q7-41 to Bell, Alexander Tomas Rivera only through M2-86 to Iqbal, and Nina Beatrice Mercer only through T9-53 to Mora. The confirmations and reconciliation share an intake event, but report different facts from different origins. There is no second attestation to any edge, no independently verified index name, and no in-file copy furnishing another minimum route. The repeated Sources across conditions are not extra evidence within either file.

shortcut_findings.heuristic: Join on exact local reference, then use the verified full name and signed predicate.
shortcut_findings.result: Succeeds on all three edges in both conditions, including T9-53. Q7-41, M2-86, and T9-53 are explicit links in the evidence, not guesses from names. k9t2 is unnecessary to this join.

shortcut_findings.heuristic: Treat the display name as the exact full name, or compare it by exact string equality to the reconciled name.
shortcut_findings.result: Fails for every edge in both conditions. None of the display cells equals the corresponding checked full name. If the heuristic first drops middle names, it gets incidental exact short-form matches for “Alexandra Rivera” in F0 and “Nina Mercer” in both conditions. It still does not match “Alex Rivera” to “Alexander Rivera,” and in F1 it also loses the Q7-41 short-form match. These matches depend on the reconciled names for comparison; none independently recovers a missing full name.

shortcut_findings.heuristic: Take the first exact display-label match, first row wins.
shortcut_findings.result: In F0 the raw labels are unique, so this retrieves the correct rows, but not exact names without reconciliation. In F1 “Alex Rivera” returns the Q7-41 row for both Rivera lookups: the Bell edge is incidentally correct if that row is resolved through c7v4, while Iqbal’s edge is misassigned to Alexandra Inez Rivera or lost if the reference mismatch is rejected. Last-row wins instead retains Iqbal’s edge and misassigns or loses Bell’s. The uniquely labelled control still retrieves T9-53. A broader first-‘Alex’ prefix search is already ambiguous in F0 and can misassign M2-86 there too.

shortcut_findings.heuristic: Use a display label as a unique person key, or merge similar names or shared surnames.
shortcut_findings.result: A raw label key has no collision in F0 but still cannot prove exact identities. In F1 it collapses two distinct identities unless it preserves both references and uses them to disambiguate. A fuzzy merger that equates Alex, Alexandra, or Alexander, or keys on Rivera, can falsely merge the two in either condition. Do not transfer a relation or infer kinship between the Riveras. Common parentage alone would not establish siblinghood, and shared children alone would not establish marriage.

shortcut_findings.heuristic: Withhold an edge whenever its display label collides.
shortcut_findings.result: A raw-label collision filter drops nothing in F0. In F1 it wrongly drops both supported Rivera edges, while the Nina Beatrice Mercer control remains. Withholding is appropriate if an exact endpoint genuinely cannot be resolved, not when the display column is ambiguous but the two reference-specific proofs are intact.

shortcut_findings.heuristic: Recover a named edge after removing a proof member by using a title, heading, short form, administrative fact, or Source ID.
shortcut_findings.result: Fails in both conditions. The confirmation titles incidentally match the signers’ exact names, which the signatures also give; they do not name the other endpoints or replace the attestations. The c7v4 section headings explicitly associate a reference with a full name and are substantive identity evidence, not independent evidence of kinship. Without the corresponding c7v4 link, no display label or other passage proves the missing exact endpoint; without the signed assertion, no remaining passage proves the relationship. The opaque Source IDs, retainer, intake procedure, and staff title add no alternative route.

shortcut_findings.heuristic: Pair confirmations and identity entries by position rather than by reference.
shortcut_findings.result: Incidentally yields all three correct named edges in both conditions because the confirmations, reconciliation sections, and index rows all occur in Q7-41, M2-86, T9-53 order. Order alone is not an identity assertion. It cannot supply a missing full name or predicate, but it can let a reader with both texts bypass the intended reference check; graph agreement alone does not show that the explicit links were used.

necessary_masks: For blinded use, show each condition separately and withhold the intended edit, expected and candidate edges, provisional rulings, and saved keys. Those materials disclose answers; they are not evidence in either advice file.

No evidentiary text needs masking for this audit. Preserve the reference-bearing headings, signatures, and display-label edit. If a separate test must rule out positional pairing, vary the relative ordering in that test while preserving the exact reference links; do not treat the original order as proof.
limitations: Supported relationship claims: Bell and Mora originate and report parentage from their own knowledge in r8h3 and b2n6; Iqbal directly reports siblinghood in j5x7. All three signed confirmations are dated 16 September 2026 and refer to the 15 September intake. They describe current relationships supported at the cut-off, not when those relationships began or their more specific legal or biological basis. There is no competing relationship attestation. The index labels do not contradict kinship. All three confirmations and c7v4 were in the cut-off file; separate receipt times are not stated.

Supported identity and intake claims: Desai reports assigning each reference in a separate 15 September intake in the presence of the person and contributor, requesting reference-only signed follow-ups for separate filing, and checking the exact names against original identification on 17 September and returning the originals. The confirmations corroborate the reference assignments and attendance, not the exact names. The originals are not reproduced in the packet. The two positive exact-name mappings contradict the proposed swapped attribution; they do not say that either proposed family relationship could never exist.

Companion register — supported administrative facts: Desai’s 17 September note records that Evelyn Park retained her for will-planning advice and agreed to preliminary information checks; the engagement date is not separately stated. k9t2 records the display entries and identifies Rowan Field as Records Assistant in the 18 September export, saved at 14:40 BST and present by the cut-off. The origin and verification of the labels are not stated. The display column is usable as a correspondence aid alongside the reference, not as an authoritative full-name field or unique lookup key. The later timestamp does not supersede Desai’s checked identities. There are no competing passages asserting a different engagement, role, or checked full name.

Companion register — unresolved: the file does not identify any specific kinship link to Evelyn Park, any relationship between the two Rivera subjects, settled drafting instructions, intended gifts or appointments, or a relevant draft or executed instrument. There is no named trust or evidenced trust office. No source by the cut-off makes those claims; Desai’s general reference to family information is context, not a competing assertion. Silence does not establish that any of these relationships, instructions, or instruments do not exist.

Questions for the adviser: How, if at all, is each person related to Park, and which relationships matter to her will? Is a particular kind of parentage or siblinghood material and in need of further evidence? What benefits or appointments does Park intend, and what existing wills, trusts, or appointment instruments should be reviewed? Can the index show verified names alongside the references? Has anything material changed since the cut-off for the 21 September meeting?
